description: Kubernetes quantity spellings both installers' readers must agree on
the PowerShell ConvertTo-TbCpuMilli/ConvertTo-TbMemBytes used to CLAIM one
grammar in a comment and diverge on `.5`, `5.`, `Pi` and `P` -- so the two
installers could reach opposite schedulability verdicts from one cluster
state (the backend#2220 twin-divergence class). A comment cannot hold two
readers together; this file is replayed through BOTH suites, so a grammar
change on one side reddens the other. `null` means 'unreadable': the reader
must refuse (empty on bash, $null on PowerShell), never guess a zero.
Hand-authored, deliberately: the inputs are written down independently of
either reader (repo rule 9's corollary). Pairs, not an object: Windows
PowerShell's ConvertFrom-Json cannot read an empty-string property name.
